Looking at this question, I need to recall specific data from studies of POLG MIRAS knock-in mice and their rotarod performance at 12 months of age.

The POLG MIRAS (missense) allele is a well-studied mutation in mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma in mice. In homozygous MIRAS knock-in mice, progressive mitochondrial dysfunction leads to declining motor coordination over time.

From the published literature on POLG MIRAS homozygous mice, at 12 months of age, these animals show a measurable but moderate decline in rotarod performance. The data from these studies indicate approximately a 20% decrease in rotarod performance compared to wild-type littermates at this age.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
